tasks.short: Grade, classify and sort products by specification

steps.what: Identify products and measure size, weight or colour against the applicable specification
Grade or classify products using measured characteristics and specification limits
Sort products into the appropriate physical destinations

tasks.design: Configure a grading table in {OPS_SYSTEM} for numeric size or weight bands from the released specification. Show the proposed destination alongside the identified measurement, while the inspector handles boundary cases, subjective colour grading and all physical sorting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Looking up repeated numeric grade bands interrupts product handling; subjective appearance is a separate problem.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instrument outputs and native rule tables can apply explicit ranges without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Correct product association, measurement uncertainty and visually ambiguous grades.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise damaged or unusual products that do not fit the numeric classification.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated band lookup; handling and authority to resolve ambiguous grades remain with the inspector.

reach.task: Investigate products clustered around a grade boundary

evidence.claim: Q-DAS O-QIS supports gauge and measuring-machine data capture and statistical process monitoring; this supports obtaining numeric inputs, not automatic physical sorting.
Explicit numeric ranges can produce a grade and destination suggestion deterministically; ambiguous appearance and physical handling remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes product identification, measurement, grading and manual placement. No conveyor, robot or automatic rejection equipment is added.

In s1 the inspector identifies product id and specification revision, presents the product to the instrument and verifies units; all 35 hours remain. Instrument firmware produces value, unit, instrument id and timestamp during that retained handling time. Unsupported instruments use manual measurement and grading without a saving.

Quality engineer already produces the released specification with characteristic, unit and inclusive or exclusive band limits outside this task. Inspector verifies the applicable bands during s1; new rule transcription and change checks are charged in the 2 incremental hours below, not assumed free.

s2 retains 12 hours for grade verification, uncertainty at limits, manual colour classification and exceptions. A missing measurement, revision or destination mapping forces manual grading, never a guessed default.
Test native rule configuration before custom code. Existing measurement runtime earns no labour saving, and s3 physical sorting retains its full share.
This task overlaps other inspection measurements; roll-ups must allocate physical measurement once.
unknowns: Fraction of grading governed solely by numeric bands
Frequency of subjective colour or defect judgements
research_questions: Can numeric band suggestions reduce lookup time while keeping wrong-destination rates unchanged?

already_counted.description: Identify and measure products, review grades and sort physically

incremental.description: Maintain grading-table revisions, device units and destination mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+12+35=82; gross 18 less upkeep 2 gives net 16. E1 scenario saves 60% of classification time for stable numeric bands only. Mostly subjective grading or unsupported instruments can leave no net gain; physical sorting never loses time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The inspector uses explicit numeric bands more quickly while retaining physical handling and ambiguous grading.
reach: Help quality engineering investigate uncertain grade boundaries
role.ambitious_version: An inspector who can explain each numeric grade from its measurement and specification while recognising products that require human judgement.

job.title: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
